facts.statement: The genus Batrachomimus contains only one species, Batrachomimus pastosbonensis, which was described and named in 2013 by Felipe C. Montefeltro, Hans C. E. Larsson, Marco A. G. de França, and Max C. Langer.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Batrachomimus pastosbonensis, with the specific name referring to the formation, which was first described and named by Felipe C. Montefeltro, Hans C. E. Larsson, Marco A. G. de França and Max C. Langer in 2013.

facts.statement: Batrachomimus lived during the Late Jurassic in the Pastos Bons Formation of northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Batrachomimus is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform known from the Late Jurassic Pastos Bons Formation of northeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: Batrachomimus had a skull measuring about 20 cm, suggesting a total body length of approximately 1 meter.
facts.quote: The skull is about 20 cm, giving an estimated total body length of about 1 m.

facts.statement: Batrachomimus possessed a narrow snout featuring wavy margins around its teeth.
facts.quote: Batrachomimus has a narrow snout with wavy margins around the teeth.

facts.statement: Batrachomimus is distinguished by the hourglass shape of its choanae, the nasal passage openings on the underside of the skull.
facts.quote: Another unique feature or autapomorphy of Batrachomimus is the hourglass-shape of its choanae, which are two holes on the underside of the skull that are openings for the nasal passages.

facts.statement: Batrachomimus lacks antorbital and mandibular fenestrae and features a backward extension of the premaxilla bone reaching the level of the fifth maxillary tooth.
facts.quote: Other distinguishing features of Batrachomimus are its lack of antorbital and mandibular fenestrae (holes in front of the eyes and at the back of the lower jaw, respectively), and a backward extension of the premaxilla bone on the snout to the level of the fifth tooth of the maxilla bone behind it.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Batrachomimus as the most basal member of the family Paralligatoridae, a group that also includes the Cretaceous Asian genera Shamosuchus and Rugosuchus.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic analysis of Montefeltro et al. (2013) placed Batrachomimus as the most basal member of the group Paralligatoridae, which also includes the genera Shamosuchus and Rugosuchus from the Cretaceous of Asia.

facts.statement: Batrachomimus lived from the Oxfordian to the Kimmeridgian stages, between 161.5 and 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian (161.5 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus name Batrachomimus means "batrachian mimic," referencing the fact that the holotype was originally misidentified as a temnospondyl, a prehistoric amphibian resembling modern frogs and toads.
facts.quote: The genus name "Batrachomimus" means "batrachian mimic" in Greek, a reference to the holotype specimen originally being identified as that of a temnospondyl, a type of prehistoric amphibian that vaguely resembles modern batrachians (frogs and toads).

facts.statement: The name Batrachomimus alludes to the evolutionary replacement of temnospondyls by crocodyliforms as dominant semi-aquatic predators during the Jurassic period.
facts.quote: The genus name also alludes to crocodyliforms replacing temnospondyls as semi-aquatic predators during the Jurassic.
